items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Clarence Page counted the money in ten parts and then asked us to give a certain amount to Rich for the gas and the time he had put in to drive us

ctx.x: luggage could be put on the side and on the fender between the hood over the left and right side of the front wheels.

So off we went in the direction of West Virginia. We arrived in Middletown, Ohio and were stopped by a motorcycle policeman who claimed that Rich had passed a car going in the same direction as we were at an intersection. I did not know anything about the rules of the road when driving a car because I could not drive. So I did not understand why we had been stopped.

The result was that Rich was fined a certain amount for which we all had to pay. Rich was not a wealthy man although he owned a Pierce Arrow car. The next trouble was with the tyres. (sic) Rich had used tyres on the car and as the weather was quite warm, one blew out in the rear. Rich patched that one up and a few miles further along the road, the other one blew out.
